newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower ahead of expiry.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly lower Thursday ahead of July's expiry, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.21 to $2.22 after settling Wednesday at $2.227 per mmBtu.
Contributing to the softer open, traders said, was early talk of lower cash prices at the Henry Hub at $2.26-2.28.
On ACCESS, July last traded one cent lower at $2.217 after American Gas Association released its storage data, showing a larger-than-expected increase of 97 bcf.

The data equated to a 19 percent increase over year-ago levels. Eastern inventories increased by 65 bcf and remained 100 bcf, or 15 percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage, which gained 10 bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by about 10 percent. Stocks in the producing region held at 54 percent above a year ago.
With the hefty AGA number, traders speculated that buyers would likely begin to pare down their injections.
"We're going to start seeing injections of 85-95 for the next two months," one trader said.
Technically, traders pegged July support at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2. Resistance was seen at $2.305 and then at $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44.
Taking a look ahead, traders pegged resistance in August at $2.25 and the recent $2.36 high. Support was seen at $2.145, $2.12 and then at the recent $2.08 low.

In Wednesday's cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices were talked little changed in the high-$2.20s. Midcon pipes also held steady in the low-teens, while New York city gate gas prices were quoted in the $2.60s.
